# PowerStation Size

> Free calculator and manufacturer-spec library for portable power stations, published by Chen Jie. Size capacity, continuous watts, and inverter surge separately. Runtime figures are estimates, not lab tests. Not medical or electrical advice.

The site answers how many watt-hours to shop for, whether an inverter can hold running watts, and whether a published peak is inverter surge or a resistive boost. Brand names identify products. They are not an endorsement.

## Primary tools

- [Portable power station calculator](https://powerstationsize.com/calculator/): Size a new station or estimate runtime for a verified model from the devices you run.
- [Homepage calculator](https://powerstationsize.com/): Same tool on the homepage.

## Decision pages

- [Battery backup for a CPAP](https://powerstationsize.com/guides/cpap-backup-power/): Dry vs heated-humidifier watt-hours, then three verified stations. Not medical advice. A power station is not a medical device.
- [Best portable power station for camping](https://powerstationsize.com/guides/camping-power-station/): 12V fridge, laptop, light, and phone load, then three verified stations that clear capacity, continuous output, and inverter surge.
- [Can a portable power station run a refrigerator?](https://powerstationsize.com/guides/can-a-portable-power-station-run-a-refrigerator/): Home fridge needs inverter surge (~1,200 W start), not a boost rating. 12V camping fridge is easier (~500 W start).
- [Watts vs watt-hours](https://powerstationsize.com/guides/watts-vs-watt-hours/): Watts are output. Watt-hours are stored energy. A 1,000 W headline is not a 1,000 Wh night.
- [How long will a 1000Wh power station last?](https://powerstationsize.com/guides/how-long-will-a-1000wh-power-station-last/): 850 Wh usable. Dry CPAP ~14.9 h. Heated humidifier ~9.2 h. Fridge ~9.9 h only if the peak is inverter surge.
- [Anker SOLIX C1000 vs BLUETTI Elite 100 V2](https://powerstationsize.com/guides/anker-solix-c1000-vs-bluetti-elite-100-v2/): Same ~1 kWh class. C1000 peak is SurgePad (resistive). Elite 100 V2 publishes inverter surge.
- [Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 vs BLUETTI Elite 100 V2](https://powerstationsize.com/guides/jackery-explorer-1000-v2-vs-bluetti-elite-100-v2/): Both publish inverter surge. Jackery is lighter (23.8 lb). BLUETTI has higher continuous watts and solar input.
- [Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 vs Anker SOLIX C1000](https://powerstationsize.com/guides/jackery-explorer-1000-v2-vs-anker-solix-c1000/): Jackery publishes inverter surge. C1000 peak is SurgePad. Completes the ~1 kWh triangle.
- [Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 vs 2000 v2](https://powerstationsize.com/guides/jackery-explorer-1000-v2-vs-2000-v2/): Same line, both surge. Spare watt-hours versus 23.8 lb vs 39.5 lb.
- [Anker SOLIX C1000 vs C1000 Gen 2](https://powerstationsize.com/guides/anker-solix-c1000-vs-c1000-gen-2/): Gen 2 lists 2,000 W continuous. Neither peak is inverter surge.

## How the numbers work

- [Methodology](https://powerstationsize.com/methodology/): Formulas, inverter efficiency 0.85, reserve 1.20, usable capacity 0.85, and known limits.
- [Inverter surge versus boost](https://powerstationsize.com/guides/surge-vs-boost/): Adjudication table. X-Boost, Power Lifting, and SurgePad are resistive boost, not inverter surge. Each row cites manufacturer wording and the date it was read. The calculator will not clear a motor start against a boost peak.
- [How to size a solar generator](https://powerstationsize.com/guides/solar-generator-sizing/): Watts vs watt-hours, and why panel wattage is not charge rate.

## Optional

- Refrigerator check pages exist at `/stations/{id}/refrigerator/` for each verified model. They use one estimated full-size fridge load. Prefer the calculator for a real appliance mix.
